summary: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Raniero Gnoli was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1950–1954) and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranu Kunwar is a scholar who pursued PhD studies at the Australian National University under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron, attested in 2026.

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017) and at Santa Clara University (attested 2012).
Raphael Kühner was a linguist who was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1821 to 1825.

Raphael von Koeber was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory (~1867–1872), Heidelberg University (~1873–1877), and the University of Jena (~1878–1881), and held a post at the University of Tokyo in 1893.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College. He worked at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Professor of Sanskrit & Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask was a Danish scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen. He held multiple posts at the University of Copenhagen, including professor of Eastern languages (1831).

Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. Attested in 2026, she holds the post of Professor (Special Invitee) at the Asiatic Society.

Ratna Handurukande is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who held lecturer posts at the University of Ceylon, in the Department of Sanskrit (attested 1970), and at the University of Peradeniya.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.

Ravi M. Gupta is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He was appointed Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University circa 2013.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Lucknow, Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He worked at the Institute of Archaeology (1986–1997) and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India until 2004.

Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and physics who studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University. He was a physics professor (1945–1986) and director (attested 2002) at Chulalongkorn University.

Raymond West was an Indologist and jurist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1887–1892), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (~1895–1907).

Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from circa 1986 to 1995.
Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg as lector for Tibetan Studies under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk, attested in 2026.

Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Washington and Yale University. She held legal academic posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
Rebecca Sundén is an Indology and Tibetology researcher who served and studied as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg, attested in 2026.

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under mentors including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University, attested between 2001 and 2006.
